rounds.fact: Ticketmaster moved a huge chunk of its ticket sales online in the late 90s, a shift that eventually made its service fees a much more visible (and criticized) part of buying tickets.
ABC News's early website tried to translate its broadcast anchors' star power onto the web, with a design that prioritized video clips even when most users were still on dial-up.
Orbitz was launched in 2001 by a group of major airlines banding together to compete directly with Expedia and Travelocity for online bookings.
Netscape's browser dominated the early web so completely that Microsoft bundling Internet Explorer with Windows to compete became the center of a landmark antitrust case.
WordPress launched in 2003 as a small blogging tool and eventually grew to power a huge share of all websites on the internet, blogs and full businesses alike.
